reviewRepairR1.boundedXmlAdmission: Before kdbxweb can consume decrypted XML, install its supported DOMParser/XMLSerializer adapter in the disposable worker using an independently version-checked maintained @xmldom/xmldom parser. Cap XML UTF-8 bytes at 2MiB before parsing, reject DTD/ENTITY declarations, then bound depth<=32 and total nodes<=20000. Reject every element carrying a true Compressed attribute before returning a DOM to kdbxweb, including inline entry/history/metadata binary nodes regardless of outer compression. KDBX4 outer compression must also be None. The actual adapter and bundled decompression paths must be instrumented with SMALL synthetic external files; library must not reach gunzip for inner binaries. If the public parser injection cannot interpose before any expansion, disable import and report PT-04 blocked; no monkey patch of internal crypto/format parser. Add the parser as one exact dependency only after registry/license/advisory verification. Never run a bomb-size probe.
reviewRepairR1.singleFlightWorker: Each live KDBX worker/session has a synchronous busy flag set before any asynchronous dispatch; reject overlapping commands rather than queueing mutable references. This covers edit/save/export/reveal/delete/restore, not just IDB writes. Never concurrently call KDBX.save on one object. If a mutating command or encryption/write fails, terminate/discard that worker and relock; only the last committed ciphertext may seed another session. Before committing/exporting, reopen the bounded output with an independent library instance in the same serialized command and verify expected synthetic contract; independent external-reader fixtures remain a separate gate.
reviewRepairR1.latchInvalidation: Add a single no-payload same-tab backend-latched event at the actual successful capability transition in src/learning/core.ts, after durable latch state is written but synchronously before probe resolution/main.ts reload. A current-value guard checks both the preview constant and present latch state before every personal-tools read/write/commit. Subscribers invalidate epochs, abort active IDB transactions, terminate workers and clear decrypted/draft view state synchronously before any dirty-note beforeunload could cancel reload. Do not rely on storage events or polling. Preserve existing capability response criteria and original route/API authorization. Include core.ts, preview.ts/main.ts call-site tests in the touched slice; main.ts need not change if event owner ordering is sufficient. Test same-tab latch with canceled reload and a pending IDB read.

dataContracts.database: dlb-personal-tools-local-v1 version 1; open requires current isInterfacePreview===true. No seed data or secrets. Stores: memberships, periods, reminders, notes, attachments, vault. UTC createdAt/updatedAt and monotonically increasing revision on owned records.
dataContracts.membership: Membership(id, service<=120, accountLabel<=120, archived, revision); Period(id, membershipId, previousPeriodId?, startDate, endDate, amountMinor, currency, reminderEmail<=254, optionalWeChatDestination, archived, revision). End is inclusive. Keep original expired period immutable on renewal: append successor atomically with unique previousPeriodId; do not advance the old expiry/cost/destination. Corrective edits have explicit confirmation/history, never masquerade as renewal.
dataContracts.membershipValidation: Strict real dates, start<=end, supported currency, finite nonnegative bounded minor units, trimmed nonempty service, bounded destination with CR/LF rejection. Annual default end uses clamped calendar-year increment; explicit edited dates are validated, not silently rewritten. Prevent overlapping active periods for one membership; retries reuse the same successor identity. Group costs by currency and period, no FX fiction. Archive never deletes history.
dataContracts.reminder: Key=(periodId, channel=email|wechat). Unique IDB key and transaction for upsert/dedup. dueDate=subtract one calendar month from inclusive endDate with target-month-end clamp; dates are date-only browser local calendar for this increment. Recompute pending due state after open/focus/day change, preserve prior attempts. State=not-configured|due-unsent|failed|delivered; delivered requires providerReceiptId+deliveredAt from an actual future provider, no UI toggle. This increment cannot produce delivered. Late/expired unsent periods remain visible; renewing must not erase the old unsent period.
dataContracts.notes: Note(id, title<=150, format=markdown|richtext, body<=100KB UTF-8, tags<=20 each<=32, archived, attachmentIds, revision, createdAt, updatedAt). Separate source format; switching editor modes creates an explicitly confirmed conversion/copy, never silently overwrites source. Independent of learning/book-linked notes. Search own title/body plaintext projection/tags; do not index the vault.
dataContracts.attachments: Owned local blobs with random stable IDs, noteId, validated MIME, safe name, size and digest. Allow only decoded PNG/JPEG/WebP <=2MiB and <=16 megapixels, and UTF-8 TXT/MD <=1MiB. Reject HTML, SVG, XML, scripts, executables, PDF, archives, data URLs and remote image fetches. Total <=10MiB per note and <=50MiB assets per DB; all count/byte limits checked before transaction commit. Note+blob changes atomic in the same DB; failed writes retain prior body and assets. Revoke created blob URLs on replacement/unmount and never persist blob: URLs.
dataContracts.noteInterchange: Import raw .md as text or versioned .notes.json with validated note metadata and bounded base64 assets, <=20MiB input and <=100 notes. Stage validation/sanitization/type sniffing before commit; reject unsafe schemas/prototype keys/duplicates with no partial writes. Export .md text or sanitized .notes.json, not executable .html; no CDN/URL imports or ZIP extractor. Use fixed extensions, strip paths/control chars, Windows reserved names and leading dots, truncate safe basename<=80 chars. Notes export is explicitly readable personal content, not the vault backup route.
dataContracts.vault: One vault row(id=primary, kdbx:ArrayBuffer, revision, updatedAt), no entry metadata/password/key/audit body in any other store. All platform/account/password/URL/notes and KDBX entry history are inside authenticated encrypted KDBX. Backups and restores are .kdbx only; never saveXml/loadXml or plaintext JSON/CSV fallback.
dataContracts.vaultEncryption: Use KDBX4 AES-256 plus standard KDBX HMAC and Argon2id v0x13. New-file KDF: 32768KiB, 3 iterations, parallelism1, 32-byte output, library-generated salts/IV; set KDBX header memory in its documented byte units. Adapter accepts only validated bounded parameters (<=65536KiB, <=6 iterations, parallelism<=2, expected output length/version/type), otherwise reject. No password normalization that breaks KeePass interoperability. Roundtrip against an independently generated synthetic KDBX fixture, not merely self-roundtrip.
dataContracts.vaultImportBounds: KDBX input/output <=10MiB, <=1000 entries and bounded fields/history. First increment writes and accepts only uncompressed KDBX4 with the supported KDF/cipher: use the library header reader to validate before decrypt/decompression, reject unsupported/compressed files without touching old data. No custom binary parser; if the chosen release cannot expose safe pre-load bounds, stop and return a library capability blocker before enabling imports. Run crypto/XML work in a disposable worker with a bounded 10s operation deadline; termination is responsiveness protection, not a claimed hard JS heap sandbox.
dataContracts.vaultConcurrency: Worker owns KDBX and credentials in memory only. Unlock input cleared immediately after handoff. A monotonic session epoch fences every unlock/read/save/import/export/reveal/copy result; capture epoch and ciphertext revision. Crypto completes outside an IDB transaction; before writing, require live epoch and transactionally compare expected revision, then commit whole ciphertext. Failed crypto/import/quota/abort/conflict keeps last committed ciphertext byte-identical. Stage restore in a separate worker/session, validate before explicit replace confirmation and atomic CAS; do not delete the live row first. Conflicts require reload/unlock, never last-writer-wins.
dataContracts.vaultLock: Lock immediately on hidden, pagehide, route leave/unmount, preview-disable/backend latch, or 2 minutes idle. Visibility resume also compares real elapsed activity time. Increment epoch, terminate worker, abort tracked pending write transactions, clear decrypted rows, search state, editor fields, reveal/copy state, master input, credentials and key references. Ignore all late completions; cross-tab lock notification contains no secret. JS cannot guarantee forensic zeroization; clear mutable byte buffers best-effort and discard references. User/device compromise and same-origin XSS remain explicit risks.
dataContracts.vaultInteractions: Reveal only by explicit control for <=15s; hide on blur/lock. Clipboard write only on user gesture and show permission failure, never success on rejection. No plaintext fallback when clipboard unavailable and no clipboard-read permission. Clearing OS clipboard is best-effort only and cannot be guaranteed or safely overwrite later user copies. URLs allow only credential-free http(s) links, no embedded auto-fetch and noopener/noreferrer. Never include decrypted fields in route params, worktab titles, analytics, screenshots or logs.

risks.risk: Index exists but properties missing, search relevance weak, tested_by empty and sourceCommit NO_GIT_COMMIT.
risks.mitigation: Targeted reads/test imports and four verified source fingerprints supplement index. No Git revision claims, no L3 semantic merge, no broad graph rebuild.

risks.risk: Host has broad unsandboxed tools; no native child-review dispatch or tool_search loader in this invocation.
risks.mitigation: Behaviorally restrict writes to the three reports, no deferred-tool calls or runtime mutations. Return plan draft to parent for mandatory independent standard review/registration; do not self-certify it.

handoff.parentActions: Review these ordinary artifacts against the frozen source, run fresh mandatory standard plan review, correct findings, and own all artifact/decision/stage booking. Resolve explicit blockers without laundering partial acceptance.
handoff.writeStop: After the three report files are written and read-only report checks finish, stop writes. No source/test/config/dependency/runtime changes are authorized by this dispatch.
